label: def:Q-value-transition
title: $\mathcal{Q}_q$-Value as Categorical Action Difference
html:
Definition. \mathcal{Q}_q-Value as Categorical Action Difference

Let \mathcal{N}(Z,N) be the normal form of a nucleus with Z protons and N neutrons, and let \mathfrak{S}_q(\mathcal{N}) be its categorical action (def:categorical-action). For a \beta^- transition \mathcal{N}(Z,N) \to \mathcal{N}(Z{+}1,N{-}1) + e^- + \bar{\nu}_e, the \mathcal{Q}_q-value is the categorical action difference between the parent and the products:

  \mathcal{Q}_q
  = 
  \mathfrak{S}_q\bigl(\mathcal{N}(Z,N)\bigr) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q\bigl(\mathcal{N}(Z{+}1,N{-}1)\bigr) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q(e) -
  \mathfrak{S}_q(\bar{\nu}_e),

with \mathfrak{S}_q(\bar{\nu}_e) = 0 since the antineutrino is the unknot. This is the primary definition. It does not assume classical energy conservation, which is the q = 1 limit; the relation between \mathcal{Q}_q and the kinetic energies of the products is the q-anomaly \delta_q treated in rem:Q-value-transition-properties. When q is fixed we write Q for \mathcal{Q}_q.

Mass-difference form. In the archimedean realisation the action of a nucleus is its mass, and the same transition is evaluated as the difference of neutral atomic masses,

  Q = M(Z, N) - M(Z{+}1, N{-}1),
  \qquad
  M(Z, N) = Z m_{\mathfrak{p}} + N m_{\mathfrak{n}} + Z m_e - B(Z, N),

where B(Z,N) is the binding energy at Hecke level k under the Bethe–Weizsäcker emergence conjecture (conj:q-integer-mass-formula). Expanding the atomic masses gives Q = m_{\mathfrak{n}} - m_{\mathfrak{p}} - m_e - \bigl(B(Z,N) - B(Z{+}1,N{-}1)\bigr). This is the form in which Q is compared with measured values; it is a realisation of the action difference, not a second definition, and its numerical content is conditional on the conjecture that supplies B.
